t:
(a) In General.—Section 6103(o) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:“(3) Taxes imposed by section 4481.—Returns and return information with respect to taxes imposed by section 4481 shall be open to inspection by or disclosure to officers and employees of United States Customs and Border Protection of the Department of Homeland Security whose official duties require such inspection or disclosure for purposes of administering such section.”. 
    (b) Conforming Amendments.—Paragraph (4) of section 6103(p) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “or (o)(1)(A)” each place it appears and inserting “, (o)(1)(A), or (o)(3)”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "inspection by or disclosure to" signals an information-sharing or consultation process. But the only recipients are officers and employees of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, a federal agency, so the sharing of tax return information stays entirely inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object, and the conforming amendment is purely technical.
fable.s: shall be open to inspection by or disclosure to officers and employees of United States Customs and Border Protection of the Department of Homeland Security whose official duties require such inspection or disclosure

opus.w: This section only lets tax return information pass from the IRS to employees of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, so the information stays inside the federal government. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue. The disclosure language may look procedural, but no party outside the federal government takes part in any decision, and the conforming amendment is purely technical.
opus.s: Returns and return information with respect to taxes imposed by section 4481 shall be open to inspection by or disclosure to officers and employees of United States Customs and Border Protection of the Department of Homeland Security
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "inspection by or disclosure to" sounds like an outside party getting access to a federal process. That fails here. The disclosure goes only to officers and employees of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, which is a federal agency, so no one outside the federal government is involved in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes federal employees (Customs and Border Protection officers) to access tax information for administrative purposes. All actors involved are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination or access. There is no consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards involving non-federal members.
qwen_chat.s: Returns and return information with respect to taxes imposed by section 4481 shall be open to inspection by or disclosure to officers and employees of United States Customs and Border Protection of the Department of Homeland Security whose official duties require such inspection or disclosure for purposes of administering such section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing Customs and Border Protection officers to inspect tax returns involves "participation" because it involves different government entities interacting. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is *not* participation. Furthermore, this section is about internal administrative access to data, not about consulting with outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts) before making a decision.
